mainTopic: Moving מוקצה indirectly (straw on a bed, the clothes press משנה) and a series of practical שבת precautions about mud, water and leveling holes
overview: The amud opens by finishing the גמרא's discussion of moving animal food on שבת: a 'bad mouth' animal that eats anything is a donkey, and its leftovers may be given to a picky cow. A new משנה then rules that straw on a bed is moved only with the body, unless it is animal food or has a pillow or sheet on it. The same משנה says a homeowner's clothes press may be loosened but not tightened, and a launderer's press may not be touched, though רבי יהודה allows fully loosening one that was already partly loosened before שבת. The גמרא quotes רב נחמן, who forbids pulling a radish out of the ground when that moves the dirt. The school of רב uses the straw משנה to disprove him, concluding that טלטול מן הצד לא שמיה טלטול: moving something indirectly does not count as moving. Then comes a series of practical rulings about peppers crushed with a knife handle, drying off after bathing, wiping mud off the foot, sitting at the entrance of a מבוי, setting down a barrel, and stuffing a rag into a jug. The amud ends with rules for removing mud from clothing and shoes: rub a garment only from the inside, and scrape only a new shoe, not an old one.

steps.title: The animal in the earlier case slobbers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier explanation. The animal in that case has slobber, which makes its leftover food disgusting.
steps.simpleTranslation: …because it has slobber.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the last piece of an answer that began on the previous daf. It explains why food in front of a certain animal is a problem: that animal slobbers on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food covered in an animal's slobber becomes disgusting, so other animals may not want it. That is why the earlier ברייתא did not allow moving it to another animal on שבת. This sets up the next step, where 'bad mouth' will mean something different.

phrases.english: because it has slobber.
phrases.notes: Continues an answer from the previous daf (140b).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a resolution begun on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the animal in question slobbers on its food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Food in front of a slobbering animal becomes repulsive, so that ברייתא forbids moving it.

steps.title: In the other ruling, 'bad mouth' means a donkey and 'good mouth' means a cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the other ברייתא, which permits taking food from an animal with a 'bad mouth' and giving it to one with a 'good mouth.' The first is a donkey, which eats anything without choosing. The second is a cow, which is picky about what it eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what was taught, 'We may take food from in front of an animal whose mouth is bad': that means a donkey, because it does not pick and choose but just eats. 'And we may put it in front of an animal whose mouth is good': that means a cow, which picks carefully and then eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains a second ruling so that it does not contradict the first. In this ruling, 'bad mouth' means an animal that eats without choosing, not an animal that slobbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey has no slobber problem, so its leftovers are not disgusting. It is called 'bad mouthed' only because it eats everything without choosing. Food taken from a donkey is still clean, so it may be given to a picky cow on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose mouth is 'bad' (here: eats without choosing)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'bad mouth' means slobber here. In this ruling it means 'eats anything.' That is exactly why food from in front of it stays clean enough to move.
steps.whatToRemember: Food may be moved on שבת from a donkey to a cow, because a donkey does not slobber on its food. Food in front of an animal that slobbers may not be moved to another animal.

phrases.english: And that which was taught:
'We may take from in front of an animal whose mouth is bad'
refers to a donkey, which does not pick and choose but just eats.
'And we may put it in front of an animal whose mouth is good'
refers to a cow, which picks carefully and then eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of resolution to the second ruling, giving 'bad/good mouth' a different meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining terms: 'bad mouth' means eating without choosing, not slobbering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think 'bad mouth' always means an animal whose leftovers are disgusting.
steps.terutzMaskana: A donkey's leftovers are clean, so they may be given to a picky cow on שבת.

steps.title: Straw on a bed: move it with your body, unless it is clearly meant for use
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that straw lying on a bed may not be moved by hand on שבת, only with the body. If the straw is animal food, or a pillow or sheet is on it, it may be moved by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Straw that is on top of a bed: one may not move it with his hand, but he may move it with his body. And if it was animal food, or a pillow or sheet was on it, he may move it with his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on how a person may move straw lying on a bed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain straw is usually meant for burning, so it is מוקצה and may not be handled normally. Moving it with your body is not the usual way, so that is allowed. If the straw is animal food, or a pillow or sheet shows it was put there to sleep on, it is not מוקצה and may be moved by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: With his body (not the normal way of handling)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the idea that moving מוקצה with your body (טלטול מן הצד / בגופו) is treated more leniently than moving it by hand.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Straw that is on top of a bed
one may not move it with his hand,
but he may move it with his body.
And if it was animal food,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עָלָיו כַּר אוֹ סָדִין —
phrases.english: or a pillow or sheet was on it,
he may move it with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straw on a bed is moved only with the body. If it is animal food or has a pillow or sheet on it, it may be moved by hand.

steps.title: A clothes press: a homeowner's may be loosened, a launderer's may not be touched
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on a clothes press. A homeowner's press may be loosened on שבת but not tightened. A launderer's professional press may not be touched at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: A press belonging to homeowners: we may loosen it, but we may not press with it. And a press belonging to launderers: one may not touch it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a second case: a press used to flatten laundered clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loosening a homeowner's press to take out clothes is allowed. Tightening it to press clothes is forbidden, because that is like doing work on the clothing. A launderer's press is a professional tool that is used only for forbidden work, so it is fully מוקצה and may not be touched.

phrases.english: A press belonging to homeowners:
we may loosen it, but we may not press with it.
And one belonging to launderers: one may not touch it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A homeowner's press may be loosened but not tightened. A launderer's press may not be touched.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a launderer's press already loosened may be fully opened
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that if the launderer's press was already partly loosened before שבת, one may loosen it completely on שבת and take out the clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If it was loosened from ערב שבת, he may loosen all of it and slide out the garment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a dissenting opinion about the launderer's press. He permits fully opening it if it was already partly open before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids touching a launderer's press at all. רבי יהודה holds that once the press was partly loosened before שבת, finishing the job to get the clothes out is permitted. Both agree that tightening it is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Here מוּתָּר means 'loosened,' not 'permitted.' It describes the state of the press.
steps.whatToRemember: Straw on a bed: move it with your body, unless it is clearly set up for use. A homeowner's press: loosen only. A launderer's press: do not touch, unless (according to רבי יהודה) it was already partly loosened before שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If it was loosened from Shabbat eve,
he may loosen all of it and slide out the garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling on a launderer's press.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A launderer's press that was partly loosened before שבת may be fully loosened on שבת to remove the garment.

steps.title: רב נחמן on pulling a radish out of the ground
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that a radish buried wide-end-up may be pulled out on שבת, but one buried wide-end-down may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן said: This radish, if it is buried from top to bottom, it is permitted. If it is buried from bottom to top, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by quoting רב נחמן about removing a radish stuck in the ground on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wide part is on top, the radish slides out cleanly and no dirt moves. If the wide part is at the bottom, pulling it out pushes the dirt aside. Dirt is מוקצה, so רב נחמן forbids it even though the dirt is only moved indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: from top to bottom (wide end up)

phrases.english: Gemara: Rav Nachman said:
This radish,
phrases.notes: One that is buried in the ground

phrases.english: from top to bottom — it is permitted.
phrases.notes: Wide end up, so no dirt is moved when it is pulled out

phrases.english: from bottom to top — it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Wide end down, so pulling it out pushes the מוקצה dirt

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה, starting with indirect moving of מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A radish that is buried so that removing it moves the dirt may not be pulled out on שבת.

steps.title: The school of רב challenges רב נחמן from the straw משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אבא reports that the school of רב says our משנה about straw on a bed already teaches the opposite of רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אבא said: They say in the school of רב: We already learned a teaching that goes against רב נחמן. Straw on top of a bed may not be moved by hand, but it may be moved with the body. If it is animal food, or a pillow or sheet is on it, it may be moved by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our own משנה from earlier to challenge רב נחמן. The משנה is quoted again here to serve as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The straw on the bed is מוקצה, yet the משנה lets a person shift it with his body. That is moving מוקצה indirectly, which is the same thing that happens to the dirt when the radish is pulled out. So the משנה seems to permit what רב נחמן forbade.

keyTerms.meaning: the school or study hall of רב

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new משנה. It is the same משנה from step 3, quoted again because now it is being used as proof against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Abba said,
They say in the school of Rav:
We already learned not like Rav Nachman.
Straw that is on top of a bed —
one may not move it with his hand,
but he may move it with his body.
And if it was animal food,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עָלָיו כַּר אוֹ סָדִין —
phrases.english: or a pillow or sheet was on it —
he may move it with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling in step 6 using the משנה from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ban on pulling out a radish when doing so moves the dirt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits moving מוקצה straw with the body, which is indirect moving. Pushing dirt aside while pulling a radish is also indirect moving, so it should be permitted too.

steps.title: Indirect moving is not considered moving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the משנה that טלטול מן הצד does not count as moving, and it accepts this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: moving something indirectly is not called moving. Indeed, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the rule that comes out of the straw משנה and agrees that it is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that moving מוקצה indirectly, with the body or as a side effect, is not counted as forbidden moving. The repeated שמע מינה shows the גמרא accepts the proof. So the ruling does not follow רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this; also used to accept a conclusion
moving something indirectly, in an unusual way

steps.whatToRemember: טלטול מן הצד לא שמיה טלטול: moving מוקצה indirectly, for example with your body, is allowed. That is why the ruling does not follow רב נחמן's radish ban.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the basic rule for many practical questions about pushing or shifting מוקצה items without picking them up by hand.

phrases.english: Learn from this that moving from the side —
is not called moving.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ טִלְטוּל מִן הַצַּד לָא שְׁמֵיהּ טִלְטוּל. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in step 7 and ends the discussion of רב נחמן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Indirect moving of מוקצה is permitted, against רב נחמן.

steps.title: רב יהודה on crushing peppers with a knife handle
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה permits crushing peppers one at a time with a knife handle on שבת, but forbids crushing two at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: These peppers, crushing them one by one with the handle of a knife is permitted. Two at a time is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about crushing peppers on שבת in an unusual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing spices is normally like the forbidden work of grinding. Using a knife handle instead of a mortar is a change from the normal way. Even so, רב יהודה allows only one at a time, because crushing two at once looks too much like real grinding.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
These peppers,
crushing them one by one
with the handle of a knife — is permitted,
two at a time — is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected to the previous one by the idea of doing something in an unusual way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crushing peppers with a knife handle is allowed one at a time, but not two at a time.

steps.title: רבא permits crushing many peppers because of the change
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that since the person is already doing it in an unusual way, even crushing many peppers at once is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since he is changing the normal way, even many are also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with רב יהודה about the peppers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the knife handle is already enough of a change (שינוי) to take this out of forbidden grinding. Once there is a change, the number of peppers does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: since he changes the normal way

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since he changes the normal way —
phrases.notes: By using a knife handle instead of a mortar

phrases.english: even many is also permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב יהודה's limit in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the crushing is done in a changed way, any amount is permitted.

steps.title: Dry off before leaving the water
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that someone who bathes on שבת should dry himself first and only then come out, so he does not carry the water on him four אמות in a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: One who bathes in water should dry himself first and then come up, because he might come to carry the water four אמות in a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling from רב יהודה about bathing on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water drops on the body could count as an item being carried. The water and the area around it are a כרמלית, where carrying four אמות is forbidden מדרבנן. So he should dry off right away before walking out.

keyTerms.meaning: an in-between area, neither private nor public, where carrying is forbidden מדרבנן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for being careful about drying off and not carrying water when swimming or bathing on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
One who bathes in water —
should dry himself first
and then come up,
lest he come to carry
phrases.notes: The water drops on his body

phrases.english: four cubits in a karmelit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מַאן דְּסָחֵי בְּמַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate ruling from רב יהודה, on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bather must dry himself before coming out, so he does not carry the water four אמות in a כרמלית.

steps.title: Walking into the water also pushes water four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's concern about carrying water. When someone goes down into the river, he pushes water four אמות, so that should be forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then when he goes down into the water, he also pushes water four cubits with his force, and that should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reasoning of רב יהודה's rule from Step 11. If we worry about water moving four אמות, then simply entering the river should be a problem too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said a bather must dry off before leaving the water so he does not carry water four אמות in a כרמלית. The גמרא points out that walking into the river also pushes water forward four אמות. Yet no one forbids entering the water, so the worry seems inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: If so — the opening of a challenge that follows someone's logic to its end
His force, meaning an object moved by a person's push rather than carried in his hand

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כִּי קָא נָחֵית נָמֵי,
phrases.english: If so, when he goes down (into the water) also,

phrases.aramaic: קָא דָּחֵי כֹּחוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, וַאֲסִיר!
phrases.english: his force pushes (the water) four cubits, and it should be forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כִּי קָא נָחֵית נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind רב יהודה's drying-off rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's concern about carrying water four אמות in a כרמלית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If moving water four אמות is a concern, then entering the river should also be forbidden, because one's force pushes water four אמות. Yet entering is clearly not forbidden.

steps.title: No decree on water moved only by force in a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן made no גזירה about water that moves only because a person pushes it in a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding his force in a כרמלית, the רבנן did not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Water that is only pushed by a person's body in a כרמלית is not covered by the רבנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the water with water on your body is like actually carrying it. Pushing water forward as you walk in is only כֹּחוֹ, an indirect effect. Since carrying in a כרמלית is only a rabbinic prohibition, the רבנן did not extend it to this weaker, indirect kind of moving.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the רבנן) did not make a decree
An in-between area (like a river or sea) where carrying is forbidden only by the רבנן

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not cancel רב יהודה's rule. Water clinging to your body when you come out still counts as carrying. Only water you push indirectly is exempt.

phrases.english: His force in a karmelit — they did not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between direct carrying and indirect movement by force
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any water moved four אמות, even by pushing, should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only water actually carried on the body is forbidden. Water pushed by one's force in a כרמלית was never included in the גזירה.
steps.whatToRemember: Water on your body when leaving counts as carrying. Water you push while entering is only כֹּחוֹ in a כרמלית, and that is permitted.

steps.title: Wiping mud off the foot: ground yes, wall no
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב יהודה) rules that mud on one's foot may be wiped on the ground but not on a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was רב יהודה: Mud on his foot, he may wipe it on the ground, but he may not wipe it on a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new ruling about a similar everyday שבת worry. Mud on the foot may be wiped onto the ground but not onto a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No reason is given here yet. The next step will suggest that wiping mud on a wall looks like plastering, a kind of בונה.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say Rav Yehuda:
Mud that is on his foot —
he may wipe it on the ground,
but he may not wipe it on the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the same series of practical שבת rules
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mud on the foot may be wiped on the ground, not on a wall.

steps.title: A mud wall is not real building
steps.stepSummary: רבא questions the reason for forbidding the wall. If the worry is that it looks like building, smearing mud on a wall is only a field worker's crude building.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why not on the wall? Because it looks like building? But that is only the building of a field worker!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the ruling of Step 14. He shows that the likely reason for banning the wall does not hold up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumed reason is that smearing mud on a wall looks like plastering, which is part of בונה. רבא answers that adding a bit of mud this way is only the crude building of a field worker. It is not real building and does not even look like it.

keyTerms.meaning: A field worker's building — crude, not real building

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא בַּכּוֹתֶל לָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason (he may) not (wipe) on the wall?
Because it looks like building?
But that is a field worker's building!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on wiping mud on a wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only reason would be that it looks like building, but crude mud-smearing is not considered building at all.

steps.title: רבא reverses the rule: wall yes, ground no
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules the opposite. Wipe the mud on the wall, not on the ground, because wiping on the ground might lead to leveling holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: He may wipe it on the wall but not on the ground, because he might come to level out holes.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the earlier reason, רבא gives his own ruling, which flips the earlier rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wall is fine because crude mud-smearing is not building. The ground is the real concern: rubbing your foot on dirt could fill in holes and level the floor. Leveling holes is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps he will come to (do something forbidden)
To level out holes in the ground

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, wiping mud on a wall is allowed because it is not real building. Wiping it on the ground is forbidden because it might lead to leveling holes.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. אביי or רב יהודה said ground yes, wall no. רבא said the exact opposite: wall yes, ground no.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the reason behind a rule decides the rule itself. Once the building worry falls away, a different worry, leveling the ground, takes over and flips the ruling.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
He may wipe it on the wall but may not wipe it on the ground —
perhaps he will come to level out holes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the reason in Step 15, רבא offers an opposite ruling with a new reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mud may be wiped on a wall but not on the ground, because of the worry about leveling holes.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא forbids both the wall and the ground
steps.stepSummary: A new opinion is reported: מר בריה דרבינא forbids wiping mud both on the wall and on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: מר בריה דרבינא said: Both this (the wall) and that (the ground) are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a new pair of אמוראים who argue about the mud question. The first one, מר בריה דרבינא, takes the strictest view and forbids both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, אביי (or רב יהודה) forbade the wall, and רבא suggested the reason might be that it looks like building. רבא rejected that reason and forbade the ground instead, because of leveling holes. מר בריה דרבינא apparently takes both worries seriously, so he forbids both options.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, meaning both the wall and the ground.

phrases.english: It was stated:
phrases.notes: Introduces a dispute among other אמוראים.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said:
Both this and that are forbidden.
phrases.notes: "This" is the wall and "that" is the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, stricter position to the argument about the wall and the ground from steps 14 and 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wiping mud on the wall and wiping it on the ground are both forbidden.

steps.title: רב פפא permits both the wall and the ground
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא takes the opposite extreme and permits wiping mud on either the wall or the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Both this and that are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The second side of the dispute is given. רב פפא is lenient and permits both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does not accept either worry. In his view, the חכמים made no גזירה here, neither about looking like building nor about leveling holes.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on wiping mud. One forbids the wall only, רבא forbids the ground only, מר בריה דרבינא forbids both, and רב פפא permits both.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Both this and that are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the lenient side of the dispute that began in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wiping mud on the wall and wiping it on the ground are both permitted.

steps.title: How does one clean his foot according to מר בריה דרבינא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a person can do with muddy feet if both the wall and the ground are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to מר בריה דרבינא, on what may he wipe his foot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the strict view. If both places are forbidden, is there any way at all to clean your foot?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question does not attack מר בריה דרבינא. It asks for a practical solution, because it seems hard to say a person must simply stay muddy. This sets up the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: According to Mar, son of Ravina,
with what does one wipe it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא בְּמַאי מְקַנְּחִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the strict view from step 17 works in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A permitted way to clean one's foot if both the wall and the ground are forbidden.

steps.title: He wipes his foot on a beam
steps.stepSummary: Even according to מר בריה דרבינא, one may wipe his foot on a wooden beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: He wipes it on a beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is still a permitted option: wipe the mud on a beam.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam lying on the ground is not a wall, so it does not look like building. It is also not dirt, so there is no worry about leveling holes. That avoids both of the concerns that made מר בריה דרבינא forbid the wall and the ground.

phrases.english: He wipes it on a beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One wipes his foot on a wooden beam, which raises neither the building concern nor the leveling concern.

steps.title: Do not sit at the entrance of an alleyway marked by a side post
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a person should not sit at the very entrance of a מבוי marked by a לחי. An object might roll out into רשות הרבים, and he might go and bring it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person should not sit at the entrance of an alleyway with a side post, in case an object rolls away from him and he comes to bring it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new rule from רבא. It is another precaution that keeps a person away from a possible מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לחי is only a symbolic boundary, so the line between the alleyway and רשות הרבים is easy to forget. If something rolls out past the entrance, he might carry it back in from רשות הרבים without thinking. To prevent this, רבא tells him not to sit right at the entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: A side post (לחי) placed at the entrance of a מבוי so that one may carry inside it.
At its mouth, meaning at the entrance.
To bring it back, which here means carrying it from רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A person should not sit
at the entrance of an alleyway with a side post,
lest an object roll away from him
and he come to bring it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא לִיתִּיב אִינִישׁ אַפּוּמֵּיהּ דְּלִיחְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of רבא's protective גזירות, related in style to his worry about leveling holes in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not sit at the entrance of a מבוי with a לחי, in case an object rolls out and he carries it back from רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Do not set a barrel on a dirt floor
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that one should not set up or tilt a barrel into place on a dirt floor, in case he comes to level holes in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A person should not position a barrel, in case he comes to level holes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second precaution. It uses the same worry about leveling holes that he used for the mud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make a barrel stand steady on a dirt floor, a person might smooth out the dips in the ground. Leveling the ground is a form of building, so רבא forbids positioning the barrel there in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: To position or tilt something into place.
Leveling holes in the ground, which is a kind of building.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the worry about leveling holes is a consistent concern of רבא, the same reason he gave for the mud in step 16.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A person should not position a barrel,
lest he come to level holes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: לָא לִיצַדֵּד אִינִישׁ כּוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule of רבא, using the same leveling-holes concern as step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not position a barrel on a dirt floor, in case he levels holes in the ground.

steps.title: רבא: Do not stuff a rag into the mouth of a jug
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that one should not stuff a rag into the opening of a jug on שבת, because he might come to squeeze out liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A person should not stuff a rag into the mouth of a jug, because he might come to squeeze it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another rule in his series of שבת precautions. This time the worry is squeezing liquid out of a rag.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressing a rag tightly into a jug's opening squeezes liquid out of the cloth. Squeezing (סחיטה) is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת. רבא makes a protective rule (גזירה) against the whole action so that a person does not come to violate it.

keyTerms.meaning: to stuff in tightly, to press in
a rag or wad of cloth
squeezing liquid out, a forbidden act on שבת

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A person should not stuff a rag
into the mouth of a jug,
lest he come to squeezing.
phrases.notes: The rag soaks up liquid and is squeezed as it is pushed in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's series of precautionary rulings from steps 21–22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not stuff a rag into a jug's opening on שבת, for fear of סחיטה.

steps.title: רב כהנא: Rubbing mud off a garment from the inside only
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that mud on a garment may be rubbed off from the inside of the garment, but not from the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Mud that is on a person's garment, he may rub it from the inside, but he may not rub it from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא starts a new topic: how to clean mud off clothing on שבת. He permits rubbing from the inside of the garment but forbids rubbing from the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rubbing the cloth against itself to get mud out looks like laundering (מכבס), which is forbidden on שבת. Doing it from the outside is the normal way of cleaning, so it is forbidden. Doing it from the inside is unusual, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: he rubs it (rubbing the cloth together to remove dirt)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two verbs. כִּיסְכּוּס means rubbing the cloth together, and the concern is laundering. גֵּירוּר means scraping, and it appears in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Mud that is on his garment —
he may rub it from the inside
but he may not rub it from the outside.
phrases.notes: Rubbing from the outside resembles laundering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about removing mud from clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mud on a garment may be rubbed from the inside but not from the outside.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא that seems to forbid rubbing entirely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: mud on a shoe is scraped with the back of a knife, and mud on clothing is scraped with a fingernail, as long as one does not rub. It suggests this means no rubbing at all, which contradicts רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: Mud on his shoe, he scrapes it with the back of a knife. Mud on his garment, he scrapes it with a fingernail, as long as he does not rub. Doesn't this mean he may not rub at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב כהנא with a ברייתא that says 'as long as he does not rub' and asks whether that means rubbing is never allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows scraping but adds 'ובלבד שלא יכסכס', with no mention of inside or outside. Read simply, that sounds like a total ban on rubbing. That would contradict רב כהנא, who permits rubbing from the inside.

keyTerms.meaning: the back (blunt side) of a knife

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Mud that is on his shoe —
he scrapes it with the back of a knife,
phrases.notes: The blunt side is used so he does not scrape the way he normally would.

phrases.english: and that which is on his garment — he scrapes it with a fingernail,
as long as he does not rub.
Is it not that he may not rub at all?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's ruling from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's permission to rub mud off a garment from the inside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids rubbing with no qualification, which suggests a total ban that leaves no room for rubbing from the inside.

steps.title: The ברייתא only forbids rubbing from the outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's ban on rubbing refers only to the outside. Rubbing from the inside is still permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means he should not rub from the outside, but from the inside he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב כהנא by reading the ברייתא more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'שלא יכסכס' is read as referring only to the normal, outside rubbing that looks like laundering. With this reading, the ברייתא and רב כהנא agree completely.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not that…? (a suggested reading)

phrases.english: No — that he may not rub from the outside,
but from the inside (he may).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא bans only rubbing from the outside, which fits רב כהנא.
steps.whatToRemember: Mud on a garment: scraping with a fingernail is allowed, and rubbing from the inside is allowed. Rubbing from the outside is forbidden because it resembles laundering.

steps.title: Scraping a new shoe is permitted, but not an old shoe
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי, quoted through רבי אלעזר and רבי אבהו, rules that one may scrape mud off a new shoe but not off an old one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי אלעזר, in the name of רבי ינאי: One may scrape a new shoe, but not an old one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling about scraping mud off shoes, which makes a distinction based on how old the shoe is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new shoe's leather is strong, so scraping removes only the mud. An old shoe's worn leather may peel off when scraped, and that counts as smoothing (ממחק), a forbidden מלאכה. That is why scraping an old shoe is not allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a limit to the ברייתא's permission to scrape a shoe: it applies only where no leather will come off.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Elazar said
that Rabbi Yannai said:
One may scrape a new shoe,
but not an old one.
phrases.notes: Worn leather may come off, which is smoothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the ברייתא's permission to scrape a shoe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scraping mud off a new shoe is permitted, but scraping an old shoe is not.
